questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: The apparent westward movement of the Sun across the sky each day is primarily caused by the Earth's
options: revolution of the Moon around the Earth
rotation on its axis from west to east
tilting of its axis at about 23.5°
questions.explanation: The daily apparent westward movement of the Sun is caused by the Earth rotating eastward on its axis. Revolution around the Sun produces yearly changes in the Sun's position, while axial tilt produces the seasons.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: Which planet is classified as a terrestrial planet and has the shortest period of revolution around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is a rocky terrestrial planet and is closest to the Sun, so it completes one revolution in about 88 Earth days. Venus, Earth and Mars are also terrestrial but have longer orbital periods.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: A total solar eclipse can occur only during which phase of the Moon?
questions.explanation: A total solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun and casts its shadow on the Earth. This alignment can occur only at new moon, not at full moon or quarter phases.

questions.q: A Nigerian trader pays import duty on rice brought from Thailand through Apapa port. This payment is best described as
questions.explanation: Import duty is a tax imposed on imported goods, which makes it a tariff. A quota limits the quantity imported, an embargo bans trade, and a subsidy is financial support usually given to producers.

questions.q: Which mode of transport is most suitable for moving 500 tonnes of coal over 800 km from Enugu to a power station, where speed is not important but the cost per tonne-kilometre must be low?
questions.explanation: Railways are best suited to moving bulky, low-value goods such as coal over long distances at a relatively low cost per tonne-kilometre. Pipelines normally carry liquids or gases, air transport is costly, and road transport is less economical for such a large bulk load.

questions.q: If Nigeria's visible exports in a year are ₦18 trillion and visible imports are ₦22 trillion, the country has a
questions.explanation: Visible imports of ₦22 trillion exceed visible exports of ₦18 trillion by ₦4 trillion, so the balance of trade is unfavourable. A favourable balance of trade would occur when exports exceed imports; balance of payments also includes invisible and capital transactions.

questions.q: A rural district in Niger State has a mid-year population of 40,000 and records 1,200 live births in a year. What is the crude birth rate?
questions.explanation: The crude birth rate is (1,200 ÷ 40,000) × 1,000 = 30 births per 1,000 people. This uses live births and the mid-year population in the standard formula.

questions.q: The process by which a river wears away its bed by grinding rock fragments against it is called
questions.explanation: Corrasion, also called abrasion, is the grinding and scouring of a river's bed and banks by the load it carries. Attrition is the wearing down of the load itself, hydraulic action is the force of water, and solution is chemical removal.

questions.q: The gentle depositional slope found on the inner bank of a river meander is called a
questions.explanation: On the inside of a meander the current is slower, so alluvium is deposited to form a gently sloping slip-off slope. A river cliff forms on the outer eroding bank, while a gorge is a steep valley and a levee is a raised bank built by deposition during floods.

questions.q: The confluence of the River Niger and the River Benue is located in which Nigerian state?
questions.explanation: The two rivers meet at Lokoja, which is the capital of Kogi State. Kwara, Niger State and Nasarawa lie along parts of the Niger or Benue system, but neither has the actual confluence of the two rivers.

questions.q: The vegetation around Nguru in north-eastern Nigeria is generally sparse mainly because the area experiences
options: deep, fertile alluvial soils over most of the area
questions.explanation: Nguru lies in the Sahel, where annual rainfall is low and unreliable, so only drought-resistant grasses and scattered shrubs thrive. High rainfall would support denser vegetation, while high humidity and fertile alluvial soils are not widespread over most of that area.

questions.q: A characteristic feature of the coastal lowlands of Nigeria is
options: extensive mangrove swamps in the Niger Delta
continuous sand dunes and desert scrub
questions.explanation: The coastal lowlands, especially the Niger Delta, are dominated by mangrove swamps and tidal creeks. Sand dunes and desert scrub belong to arid northern areas, while high plateaus and temperate grassland are not characteristic of the Nigerian coast.

questions.q: A smallholder farmer in Nsukka wants to store dry maize for several months with little weevil damage. Which practice is most suitable?
options: Storing the maize in airtight hermetic bags
Sprinkling water on the grains before covering them
Keeping the grains in an open basket with fresh leaves
Spreading the grains on a damp floor
questions.explanation: Airtight hermetic bags reduce oxygen and prevent weevil multiplication without chemical treatment. Damp floors, fresh leaves and added water raise moisture and encourage mould and insect attack.

questions.q: A farmer in Zaria keeps 40 goats. Each goat consumes 0.5 kg of concentrate per day. If a 25 kg bag of concentrate costs ₦18,000, what is the cost of feeding the goats for 10 days, with no waste?
questions.explanation: The goats consume 40 × 0.5 = 20 kg per day, so for 10 days they need 20 × 10 = 200 kg. This is 200 ÷ 25 = 8 bags, and 8 × ₦18,000 = ₦144,000.

questions.q: Which practice is most likely to increase soil acidity on a smallholder farm in south-eastern Nigeria over time?
options: Continuous use of ammonium sulphate fertilizer
questions.explanation: Ammonium sulphate is an acid-forming fertilizer, and repeated use without liming can lower soil pH. Lime neutralises acidity, while mulching with legume residues and rotating with cowpea tend to add organic matter and nitrogen rather than increasing acidity.

questions.q: A radio programme is broadcast live from a town on longitude 25°E at 14:00 local solar time. What is the corresponding local solar time at a town on longitude 10°W?
questions.explanation: The longitude difference is 25° + 10° = 35°. Since 15° corresponds to 1 hour, 35° corresponds to 35 ÷ 15 = 2⅓ hours, or 2 hours 20 minutes. The town at 10°W is west of the town at 25°E, so its local solar time is 14:00 − 2:20 = 11:40.

questions.q: A ship travelling eastward crosses the International Date Line from longitude 179°E to 179°W on a Monday. What day is it immediately after crossing, assuming no other adjustments?
questions.explanation: When a vessel crosses the International Date Line eastward, the date is set back by one day. Monday therefore becomes Sunday immediately after crossing. Westward crossing would add a day, giving Tuesday.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure relative humidity directly at a weather station?
questions.explanation: A hygrometer measures the amount of moisture in the air and can give relative humidity. A barometer measures atmospheric pressure, an anemometer measures wind speed, and a rain gauge measures rainfall.

questions.q: The windward side of the Mambilla Highlands receives more rainfall than the leeward side mainly because the windward side experiences
options: orographic lifting and cooling of moist air
reduced friction over the highland surface
strong Coriolis deflection of the wind
subsidence and warming of dry air
questions.explanation: Moist air forced to rise over the highlands cools, condenses and produces orographic rain on the windward side. The leeward side lies in the rain shadow, where descending air warms and dries, while Coriolis deflection and reduced friction do not directly cause the rainfall difference.

questions.q: A student in Ibadan tests a mineral specimen that is very soft, can be scratched by a fingernail, and feels greasy when rubbed between the fingers. Which mineral is the specimen most likely to be?
questions.explanation: Talc has a hardness of 1 and a characteristic greasy or soapy feel, so a fingernail easily scratches it. Gypsum is also soft but is not greasy, while calcite and quartz are harder.

questions.q: Which mineral is the chief raw material used in manufacturing cement at Obajana and other Nigerian cement plants?
questions.explanation: Limestone is the main raw material that is heated to produce cement clinker. Gypsum is added in small amounts to control setting, while bauxite and iron ore are not the chief raw material for cement.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1:20,000, two villages are 9.5 cm apart. What is the straight-line ground distance between them?
questions.explanation: Multiply the map distance by the scale: 9.5 × 20,000 = 190,000 cm. Converting to metres and kilometres gives 1,900 m, which is 1.9 km.

questions.q: A rectangular forest is measured as 7.4 cm by 4.5 cm on a map with scale 1:50,000. What is the actual area of the forest?
questions.explanation: The map area is 7.4 × 4.5 = 33.3 cm². At 1:50,000, 1 cm represents 0.5 km, so 1 cm² represents 0.25 km²; the actual area is 33.3 × 0.25 = 8.325 km².

questions.q: A coastal community in Bayelsa State is losing land to wave action after many mangrove trees were cleared. Which action would most directly help reduce the coastal erosion?
options: Dumping refuse on the beach to create land
Building houses closer to the shoreline
Replanting mangrove trees along the shoreline
Burning cleared mangrove wood for fuel
questions.explanation: Mangrove roots trap sediment and reduce wave energy along the shore, so replanting them directly protects the coast. Burning the remaining trees or building closer to the sea would worsen exposure, while refuse dumping is not a sound erosion-control measure.

questions.q: Which farming practice in the Sahel is most likely to increase wind erosion of the soil?
questions.explanation: Overgrazing removes protective vegetation and tramples the soil surface, leaving it exposed to wind. Shelter belts and manure application help protect or improve the soil, and terracing mainly controls erosion on slopes.

questions.q: A cotton ginnery in northern Nigeria is best located near cotton-growing areas mainly because the raw cotton is
options: available only during a short season each year
perishable and spoils quickly after harvesting
bulky and loses weight after ginning
processed into a product that is much heavier than raw cotton
questions.explanation: Raw cotton is bulky, and ginning removes seeds, so the processed cotton weighs less. Locating the ginnery near the farms reduces the cost of transporting the bulky raw material; cotton is not a highly perishable crop.

questions.q: Which of the following is a renewable natural resource in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is naturally replenished and can be used continuously without being depleted. Crude oil, coal and natural gas are fossil fuels formed over long geological periods and are therefore non-renewable.

questions.q: The reddish colour common to many tropical soils in Nigeria is chiefly caused by the accumulation of which substance?
questions.explanation: Weathering in warm, humid conditions releases iron compounds from parent rocks, and oxidation gives many tropical soils a red or reddish-brown colour. Calcium carbonate and sodium salts are associated more with drier or poorly drained areas, while humus darkens topsoil rather than producing a red colour.

questions.q: The presence of Guinea savanna in central Nigeria is best explained by which climatic condition?
options: rainfall below 500 mm with a short wet season
low evaporation with permanently waterlogged soils
moderate rainfall with a marked dry season
questions.explanation: Guinea savanna occurs in areas with moderate annual rainfall and a distinct dry season, which supports tall grasses and fire-resistant trees. Heavy rainfall throughout the year favours forest, while very low rainfall and permanent waterlogging describe different environments.

questions.q: Mangrove vegetation in the coastal swamps of the Niger Delta is specially adapted to which set of conditions?
questions.explanation: Mangroves tolerate salt and can grow in muddy, waterlogged coastal flats, where special roots help them obtain air and remain stable. Dry upland soils, frosty highland air and thin limestone soils do not describe the Niger Delta swamp environment.

questions.q: A settlement whose houses are arranged mainly along both sides of a major highway is best described as a
questions.explanation: A linear settlement develops in a line, often following a road, river or valley, because buildings seek access to the route. A nucleated settlement is clustered around a focus, a dispersed settlement is widely scattered, and a conurbation is formed by the merging of several urban areas.

questions.q: The concentration of banks, insurance offices and large retail shops in the central business district of Lagos is best explained by
options: low population density and quiet surroundings
high accessibility and large customer flow
questions.explanation: The central business district has the greatest accessibility and attracts many customers, so commercial activities that need high footfall concentrate there. Land values in such areas are usually high rather than cheap, and the area is densely developed rather than quiet.

questions.q: The early growth of Onitsha as a major market town was favoured mainly by its location as a
options: terminus of the groundnut railway from Kano
route focus at a crossing point of the River Niger
deep-water seaport on the Atlantic coast
centre of tin mining on the Jos Plateau
questions.explanation: Onitsha developed as a trading centre because routes converged on the River Niger crossing point, encouraging the exchange of goods. It is not a deep-water Atlantic seaport, a tin-mining centre, or the groundnut railway terminus from Kano.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: A ship at longitude 30°E records local time as 12.00 noon. What is the local time at longitude 15°W?
questions.explanation: Longitude 15°W is 45° west of 30°E. Since the Earth turns through 15° in one hour, the time difference is 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours; places to the west have earlier local time, so 12.00 noon minus 3 hours gives 9.00 a.m.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: The occurrence of the seasons is caused mainly by
options: changes in the Earth's distance from the Moon
the movement of the Sun around the Earth
the tilt of the Earth's axis as it revolves around the Sun
the rotation of the Earth on its axis
questions.explanation: The Earth's axis is tilted, so as the Earth revolves around the Sun different latitudes receive more direct sunlight at different times of the year. Rotation causes day and night, while the Sun does not revolve around the Earth.

questions.q: A Nigerian exporter sends manufactured goods through Lagos in containers. The main advantage of using containers in international trade is that they
options: reduce handling time and loss of goods through pilferage
remove the need for customs inspection
increase the speed of the carrying vessel
questions.explanation: Containers allow goods to be packed once and moved quickly between ship, rail and road, reducing labour, damage and theft. Customs inspections and insurance remain necessary, and containerisation does not make the vessel itself travel faster.

questions.q: If Nigeria's visible exports are greater than its visible imports, the country is said to have a
questions.explanation: The balance of trade compares visible exports with visible imports; when exports exceed imports, the balance is favourable or in surplus. The balance of payments is broader because it includes invisible items as well as visible trade.

questions.q: In a town, there are 24,500 males and 25,500 females. What is the sex ratio of the town, expressed as males per 100 females?
questions.explanation: The sex ratio is (24,500 ÷ 25,500) × 100 ≈ 96.1, so there are about 96 males for every 100 females. The value of 104 would result from dividing the female population by the male population by mistake.

questions.q: A rural local government area recorded 2,400 births, 900 deaths, 700 immigrants and 1,300 emigrants in one year. What was the total change in its population?
questions.explanation: Natural increase is 2,400 − 900 = 1,500, while net migration is 700 − 1,300 = −600. Total population change = 1,500 + (−600) = +900 persons, an increase.

questions.q: A stream emerging from a steep mountain front onto a broad lowland deposits coarse sediment in a fan-shaped form. This occurs mainly because the stream's
options: load is carried away by strong wave action
fine material is removed by wind deflation
discharge increases rapidly as it leaves the mountain
questions.explanation: A fan-shaped deposit at the foot of a mountain front is an alluvial fan. When the stream reaches the lowland, its gradient and velocity fall suddenly, so its carrying capacity drops and coarse sediment is deposited. Wave action and wind deflation do not account for this fluvial landform.

questions.q: The bouncing movement of sand grains along a river bed by turbulent water is called
questions.explanation: Saltation is the intermittent bouncing or hopping of sand-sized particles along a river bed. Traction involves larger particles rolling or sliding, while suspension carries fine material within the water.

questions.q: In coastal areas, sea spray leaves salt crystals in rock cracks; when the crystals grow, they exert pressure and break the rock. This process is known as
questions.explanation: Salt weathering occurs when salt crystals grow in cracks and exert pressure that flakes or breaks the rock. Carbonation acts mainly on limestone, hydrolysis alters silicate minerals, and oxidation affects iron-bearing minerals.

questions.q: The Obudu Plateau, noted for its cool climate and cattle ranching, is located in which Nigerian state?
questions.explanation: The Obudu Plateau is in Cross River State, near the Cameroon border. Plateau State contains the Jos Plateau, while Taraba and Adamawa lie further north-east.

questions.q: The River Benue enters Nigeria from which neighbouring country?
questions.explanation: The Benue rises in the Adamawa Highlands of Cameroon and enters Nigeria near Yola before flowing west to join the Niger. Chad, Niger and Benin do not form its source area.

questions.q: A farmer in Ogun State buys four 50 kg bags of urea at ₦42,000 per bag and applies them evenly on an 8-hectare field. What is the fertilizer cost per hectare?
Which cropping practice is most effective for restoring nitrogen in a degraded maize field on a smallholder farm in Kaduna State?
options: Deep ploughing the field after each rainy season
Rotating maize with a legume such as cowpea
Burning all crop residues after every harvest
Continuously planting sole maize on the same plot
questions.explanation: Legumes such as cowpea form root nodules with nitrogen-fixing bacteria, which add nitrogen to the soil when rotated with maize. Continuous maize and residue burning deplete organic matter and nitrogen, while deep ploughing does not restore nitrogen.

questions.q: An aircraft leaves Port Harcourt at 10:15 local time (GMT+1) and lands in Accra after 1 hour 20 minutes. Accra uses GMT. What is the local time of arrival in Accra?
questions.explanation: Convert the Port Harcourt departure to GMT: 10:15 local time at GMT+1 is 09:15 GMT. Adding the 1 hour 20 minutes flight time gives 10:35 GMT, and Accra uses GMT, so its local arrival time is 10:35. The answer 11:35 comes from adding the flight time without first converting from Port Harcourt time to GMT.

questions.q: Two towns are on the equator. One is on longitude 20°W and the other is on longitude 70°E. If the local solar time at 20°W is 07:00, what is the local solar time at 70°E?
questions.explanation: The longitudinal difference between 20°W and 70°E is 20° + 70° = 90°. At 15° per hour, 90° corresponds to 6 hours. The eastern town at 70°E is ahead of the western town, so 07:00 + 6 hours = 13:00.

questions.q: A hygrometer records a dry-bulb temperature of 30°C and a wet-bulb temperature of 24°C. What is the best interpretation of these readings?
options: The relative humidity is high because the wet-bulb thermometer is below the dry-bulb thermometer.
The air is saturated because the wet-bulb thermometer is cooler than the dry-bulb thermometer.
The dew point is above 30°C because the wet-bulb is 24°C.
The air is relatively dry because the wet-bulb depression is large.
questions.explanation: A wet-bulb reading lower than the dry-bulb reading shows that evaporation is cooling the wet bulb, and the size of the depression gives a measure of how dry the air is. A depression of 30°C − 24°C = 6°C is large, so the air is relatively dry. If the air were nearly saturated, the two readings would be much closer together.

questions.q: Lagos, on the coast, usually has a smaller daily temperature range than Ibadan, which is inland at a similar latitude. Which factor best explains this?
options: Harmattan winds affect Lagos more than Ibadan.
Ibadan is farther north and therefore receives more direct sunlight.
Lagos is at a higher altitude, so its temperature changes less.
The sea moderates temperature because water has a higher specific heat capacity than land.
questions.explanation: Lagos and Ibadan are at similar latitudes, so the main difference comes from Lagos being beside the sea. Water has a higher specific heat capacity than land, so it warms and cools more slowly and reduces the daily temperature range. Inland Ibadan heats and cools more rapidly, giving a larger daily range.
